title: Paraphrase of Ecclesiastes
author: Gregory Thaumaturgus
edition: MGR Greek (TLG 2063.006 / Documenta Catholica Omnia), PG 10.987-1017; checked against the Opera omnia print (Paris, 1622)
blurb: Gregory Thaumaturgus retells the whole of Ecclesiastes in Solomon's voice: human affairs are empty, pleasure and wealth never satisfy, and the book ends with its charge to fear God and keep His commandments, for every person will be judged. A fresh English translation from the Greek.
era_note: Third-century paraphrase of Ecclesiastes transmitted under Gregory Thaumaturgus.
first_english_note: Prior English exists (Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 6, public domain); this is a fresh English translation from the Greek.

text_history.method: English translated from the Greek of the MGR / Documenta Catholica Omnia transcription (TLG 2063.006, from PG 10), read from its page images. From Ecclesiastes 1:13 to the end, each passage was also checked against the Greek and Latin columns of the Opera omnia print (Paris, 1622). The older Ante-Nicene Fathers English was used only as a sense check for the opening section.

witnesses.name: Locked Greek of the opening section
Opera omnia, Greek and Latin (Paris: Sonnius, Morel and Cramoisy, 1622), page images

joins.note: The transcription brackets οὐ as an editor's supplement; the 1622 print has it as text ('there is no need to wonder'), and the English follows the 1622 print.
The transcription's χόρος is read as κόρος ('fill, satiety') with the 1622 print.
The transcription's πλέοντι is read as πλέον τι ('anything more') with the 1622 print.
The transcription prints ἀλλὰ μή with the editor's conjecture μήν; the English follows μήν ('Moreover'), as the 1622 Latin does.
The transcription's ἂ is read as the relative ἃ ('what I said before'), as the 1622 Latin requires.
Small typing and accent errors in the transcription are corrected from the 1622 print.
